assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
this is a fail-closed screening heuristic, not a legal determination; liability calls are owned by counsel
real-person identification and an upstream verifiability-tag pipeline are available as inputs
the actual audience and medium of distribution are known so the reasonable-viewer and jurisdiction analyses apply
exclusions: final legal liability and damages determinations (owned by qualified counsel)
copyright substantial-similarity and fair-use adjudication (routed to compliance/counsel)
investigative fact-checking and primary-source truth verification

competency_questions.question: How are the candidate item, its identifiable real targets, and the controlling reasonable-viewer reading captured?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAIM_INTAKE builds the target inventory and REASONABLE_VIEWER_TEST sets the interpretive lens

competency_questions.question: By whose interpretation is meaning judged, and how is protected opinion/parody distinguished from an assertion of fact?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REASONABLE_VIEWER_TEST, OPINION_VS_FACT and SATIRE_PARODY_SAFE_HARBOR fix the reasonable-viewer and provable-fact tests

competency_questions.question: How does claim verifiability control whether material may be framed as fact or only as attributed opinion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERIFIABILITY_TAGS gates factual framing and POLITICAL_NEWS_RISK applies it to real-news juxtapositions

competency_questions.question: What is the operative opinion-versus-fact test and how are the core defamation elements applied?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OPINION_VS_FACT applies the Milkovich provable-implication test feeding DEFAMATION_ELEMENTS

competency_questions.question: When does the satire/parody safe harbor apply, and how is non-literal framing made visible to the viewer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATIRE_PARODY_SAFE_HARBOR sets the no-reasonable-belief test that NON_LITERAL_FRAMING operationalizes

competency_questions.question: How are the four defamation elements and the distinct false-light tort screened?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFAMATION_ELEMENTS scores the elements and FALSE_LIGHT catches highly-offensive false impressions

competency_questions.question: How is false-association/endorsement risk distinguished from defamation and false light, and detected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FALSE_ASSOCIATION flags implied endorsement/affiliation as a distinct misappropriated-identity exposure

competency_questions.question: How does the system prevent depicting a real person committing acts they did not commit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FABRICATED_WRONGDOING enforces the bright-line prohibition on invented wrongdoing

competency_questions.question: How does plaintiff status set the fault tier and engage the actual-malice standard within US breathing space?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PUBLIC_FIGURE_STATUS classifies the target, ACTUAL_MALICE applies Sullivan, and US_FIRST_AMENDMENT_FRAME bounds the space

competency_questions.question: How is the hazard of linking a real person to real political/news events screened?
How is the scope-FP6 requirement enforced that real-person jokes be visibly non-literal and never asserted as fact?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NON_LITERAL_FRAMING forces salient visible non-literal cues or fails closed before RISK_AGGREGATION

competency_questions.question: How are US and Indian (criminal+civil) defamation regimes applied and reconciled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: US_FIRST_AMENDMENT_FRAME and INDIA_DEFAMATION encode the two jurisdictional standards

competency_questions.question: How are per-tort and per-jurisdiction signals aggregated into a fail-closed pass/block/needs-review verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RISK_AGGREGATION fuses signals by max-severity, SCREEN_VERDICT emits the verdict, and FAIL_CLOSED_DEFAULT defaults uncertainty restrictively

competency_questions.question: When are items escalated to counsel, and how is each decision made explainable and reproducible?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COUNSEL_ESCALATION routes review items to counsel without the screen ruling on liability and AUDIT_TRACE records full provenance

glossary.definition: a false statement of fact, communicated to a third party, that identifies and harms the reputation of a real person
publicity placing a real person in a false light that is highly offensive to a reasonable person, even without a literally false statement
implying that a real person or brand endorses, sponsors, or is affiliated with content when they are not
knowledge that a statement was false or reckless disregard for whether it was false, required for public officials and public figures
the protection for parody that could not reasonably be interpreted as stating actual facts about a real person
the Milkovich test: a statement is actionable if it implies an objectively verifiable, and provably false, factual assertion
the hypothetical ordinary member of the actual audience whose interpretation, not the author's intent, governs the analysis
an evidentiary status label (VERIFIED, REPORTED, ALLEGED, RUMOR) controlling whether a claim may be framed as fact
the policy that uncertainty, abstention, or missing evidence defaults to the restrictive outcome (block or review), never to pass
the screening output: PASS, BLOCK, or NEEDS-REVIEW, distinct from any legal liability determination

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for defamation, false-light, and false-association screening of generated jokes and derived scenes about real people, informed by US First Amendment defamation doctrine, the Restatement (Second) of Torts, the Lanham Act, and Indian defamation law; no supplied dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: New York Times Co. v. Sullivan, 376 U.S. 254 (1964) (actual malice); Hustler Magazine, Inc. v. Falwell, 485 U.S. 46 (1988) (parody no-reasonable-belief); Milkovich v. Lorain Journal Co., 497 U.S. 1 (1990) (opinion vs provable fact); Gertz v. Robert Welch, Inc., 418 U.S. 323 (1974) (no false idea; public/private figures); Restatement (Second) of Torts s652E (false light); Lanham Act s43(a), 15 U.S.C. s1125(a) (false endorsement/association); India IPC s499/s500 and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 s356 (criminal+civil defamation)

nodes.definition: Capture the candidate joke or derived scene together with every real person, brand, or institution it names or visually depicts, plus the literal surface meaning a viewer would extract, so screening operates on an explicit identified-target inventory rather than on the author's intent.

excluded: fully fictional characters with no real referent

outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: entity-recognition coverage or the definition of an identifiable real target changes

pros.claim: An explicit target inventory is the precondition for every downstream test: identification is the first defamation element and the gate that distinguishes a real-person risk from harmless fiction
pros.example: a parody scene naming a sitting senator and showing a recognizable caricature is flagged as identifying that senator

cons.claim: Over-identification flags incidental or coincidental name matches that no viewer would tie to the real person, inflating false positives
cons.example: a common surname shared with a celebrity flagged as if it depicts the celebrity

failure_modes: a real target depicted via context/likeness but not named is missed
intent treated as a substitute for the viewer's reading
acceptance_tests: every real person named or recognizably depicted is in the inventory with the literal surface reading recorded
revisit_triggers: entity recognition model updated
a missed real-target identification is found in audit

nodes.definition: Establish the controlling interpretive lens: how a reasonable viewer of the actual audience and medium would understand the joke or scene, since defamation, false light, and the parody safe harbor all turn on audience interpretation, not author intent or a hyper-literal parse.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: case law or platform norms shift what a reasonable viewer is taken to understand

pros.claim: Anchoring on the reasonable viewer matches the legal standard across defamation, false light, and parody, so the screen approximates the test a court would apply
pros.example: Falwell turned on whether the parody could reasonably be read as stating actual facts about Falwell

cons.claim: 'Reasonable viewer' is context-dependent and contested; the same item reads differently to a satire audience than to a news audience
cons.example: an Onion-style headline is obvious to its readers but reposted out of context looks factual

failure_modes: a niche-audience reading assumed for a general audience
literalism overrides obvious contextual non-literal cues
acceptance_tests: the verdict cites how the reasonable viewer of the actual medium/audience would read the item, not the author's intent
revisit_triggers: audience/medium of distribution changes
a contextual-stripping repost incident is observed

nodes.definition: Tag every factual proposition embedded in or implied by the item by evidentiary status: VERIFIED, REPORTED, ALLEGED, or RUMOR. Only VERIFIED and REPORTED claims may inform factual framing; ALLEGED and RUMOR material must be rendered as visibly attributed opinion, never as the screen's own assertion of fact.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the verifiability taxonomy or sourcing policy changes

pros.claim: Gating factual framing on verifiability tags operationalizes the truth defense: only well-sourced facts can ground a factual claim, and unsourced material is forced into the protected-opinion lane
pros.example: an ALLEGED corruption rumor is rendered as 'critics claim' opinion, not as 'X took a bribe'

cons.claim: Tag quality depends on the upstream source pipeline; a mis-tagged RUMOR as VERIFIED imports a false fact straight into factual framing
cons.example: a fabricated 'report' tagged REPORTED legitimizes a non-existent event

failure_modes: RUMOR silently promoted to factual framing
an implied factual claim left untagged
acceptance_tests: no ALLEGED or RUMOR proposition appears as an unattributed assertion of fact in the output framing
revisit_triggers: sourcing taxonomy revised
a mis-tagged claim reaches factual framing

nodes.definition: Classify each statement about a real target as protected pure opinion / rhetorical hyperbole or as an assertion (or implication) of objectively verifiable fact, applying Milkovich: there is no blanket opinion exemption; the dispositive question is whether the statement implies a provably false factual assertion.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the opinion/fact dividing test or its precedent shifts

pros.claim: The Milkovich provable-implication test is sharper than a naive opinion label: it catches 'in my opinion X is a thief', which implies undisclosed defamatory facts and is actionable
pros.example: 'I think the mayor embezzled funds' implies a verifiable embezzlement and is not protected as opinion

cons.claim: The boundary between figurative hyperbole and implied fact is genuinely fuzzy; aggressive classification can chill protected rhetorical exaggeration
cons.example: 'the landlord is a snake' is non-actionable hyperbole, not a factual zoological claim

failure_modes: implied-fact statements waved through as 'just opinion'
obvious hyperbole mis-scored as a factual claim
acceptance_tests: each statement about a real target is labeled opinion/hyperbole or implied-fact, with the provable-falsity rationale recorded
revisit_triggers: Milkovich-line precedent revisited
an implied-fact slips through as opinion in audit

nodes.definition: Determine whether the item qualifies for the satire/parody safe harbor: per Hustler v. Falwell, parody is protected when it could not reasonably have been interpreted as stating actual facts. The safe harbor requires that the non-literal nature be evident to the reasonable viewer, not merely intended by the author.

excluded: whether the parody is funny or in good taste

outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the parody safe-harbor standard or its evidentness requirement changes

pros.claim: The safe harbor is the principled exit for genuine parody: an outrageous, self-evidently fictional scene about a public figure is protected even if offensive, exactly as in Falwell
pros.example: an absurd cartoon clearly framed as satire of a politician's policy is safe-harbored

cons.claim: The harbor collapses when satire is dry, deadpan, or stripped of context: 'Poe's law' cases read as literal and lose protection despite satirical intent
cons.example: a deadpan fake-quote that omits any satire signal can be taken as a real statement

failure_modes: author-intended satire with no viewer-visible non-literal cue
deadpan fabrication mistaken for safe-harbored parody
acceptance_tests: safe harbor is granted only when explicit, viewer-visible non-literal cues make a factual reading unreasonable
revisit_triggers: parody standard revisited
a deadpan item is wrongly safe-harbored in audit

nodes.definition: Apply the core defamation test to each statement about a real target: (1) a false statement of fact, (2) published/communicated to a third party, (3) of and concerning an identifiable plaintiff, (4) causing reputational harm, with the requisite fault. A statement clears defamation risk only if at least one element provably fails.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the elements of the defamation tort or fault standards change

pros.claim: Decomposing into elements makes the screen auditable: a statement that is pure opinion fails element (1) and is cleared on a recorded, specific ground, not a vibe
pros.example: a clearly figurative insult fails the false-statement-of-fact element and clears

cons.claim: Element analysis can give false comfort: an item may clear one jurisdiction's elements yet be actionable under another's stricter standard
cons.example: a statement non-defamatory in the US may breach India's broader defamation rules

failure_modes: clearing on a single weak element while another element is plainly met
harm element assumed absent for a per-se defamatory imputation
acceptance_tests: each statement is scored against all four elements and clears only when at least one element provably fails, with the failing element named
revisit_triggers: fault-standard precedent changes
a per-se defamatory imputation cleared in audit

nodes.definition: Screen for the false-light tort per Restatement (Second) of Torts s652E: publicity that places a real person in a false light highly offensive to a reasonable person, with knowledge of or reckless disregard for the falsity. False light reaches misleading IMPRESSIONS that are not literally false statements, so it catches material that survives a strict defamation parse.

excluded: jurisdictions that reject false light as duplicative of defamation

outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the false-light tort's elements or its offensiveness threshold change

pros.claim: False light catches true-statement-but-false-impression cases defamation misses, e.g. a real photo placed beside an unrelated scandal headline implying involvement
pros.example: a real person's photo captioned to imply they attended an event they never did

cons.claim: Several US states reject false light as redundant of defamation, so screening it can over-flag where it provides no independent cause of action
cons.example: a state that has abolished false light treats the same facts only under defamation

failure_modes: a misleading juxtaposition cleared because no statement is literally false
offensiveness judged from the author's tolerance not a reasonable person's
acceptance_tests: any highly-offensive false impression about a real person is flagged even when no statement is literally false
revisit_triggers: a false-light-recognizing vs rejecting jurisdiction is targeted
a misleading-impression item cleared in audit

nodes.definition: Screen for false association / false endorsement: implying that a real person or brand endorses, sponsors, is affiliated with, or authored the content when they do not, grounded in Lanham Act s43(a). This is distinct from defamation: the harm is misappropriated commercial identity and consumer confusion, not reputational falsity.

excluded: nominative fair use of a mark

outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: false-endorsement or right-of-publicity standards change

pros.claim: Catching implied endorsement prevents a joke from reading as a real celebrity or brand backing the content, which is a confusion/right-of-publicity exposure separate from any reputational harm
pros.example: a generated scene showing a celebrity using a product implies a paid endorsement that never existed

cons.claim: Nominative reference to a brand or person for commentary or parody is often lawful; over-flagging suppresses legitimate critical or comparative speech
cons.example: naming a brand to criticize it is nominative fair use, not false association

failure_modes: nominative parody flagged as endorsement
implied affiliation cleared because no explicit endorsement words appear
acceptance_tests: any implication that a real person/brand endorses or is affiliated with the content is flagged unless an explicit disclaimer removes the confusion
revisit_triggers: right-of-publicity or Lanham standard changes
an implied-endorsement item cleared in audit

nodes.definition: Enforce the hard prohibition that the item must never depict a real, identifiable person committing acts they did not actually commit -- crimes, professional misconduct, abuse, or other wrongdoing -- because invented wrongdoing is a paradigm false statement of fact and false light, independent of comedic framing.

included: invented crimes/misconduct by a real person
excluded: depicting genuinely VERIFIED wrongdoing already on the public record

outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the fabricated-wrongdoing prohibition or its narrow parody exception changes

pros.claim: A bright-line block on fabricated wrongdoing eliminates the highest-severity defamation exposure, since invented criminal acts are defamatory per se and rarely survive any safe harbor
pros.example: a scene showing a named executive accepting a bribe that never happened is blocked outright

cons.claim: An absolute rule can over-block self-evident absurdist parody where no reasonable viewer believes the act occurred, conflicting with the Falwell safe harbor
cons.example: an obviously cartoonish scene of a politician fighting a dragon is not a factual wrongdoing claim

failure_modes: fabricated misconduct passed under a comedic label
doctored 'evidence' treated as verified
acceptance_tests: no real person is depicted committing a non-VERIFIED act unless a self-evident parody cue makes a factual reading unreasonable and it is escalated for review
revisit_triggers: the narrow parody carve-out is invoked
a fabricated-wrongdoing item cleared in audit

nodes.definition: Classify each real target as a public official, all-purpose public figure, limited-purpose public figure, or private individual, because the applicable fault standard and the breathing space for commentary depend on this status (Gertz), with private individuals entitled to greater protection.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the public-figure classification doctrine changes

pros.claim: Status classification is the dial that sets the risk tier: a private individual gets the strictest protection, so misclassifying them as public would dangerously relax the screen
pros.example: a private citizen briefly in the news is not an all-purpose public figure and keeps strong protection

cons.claim: Public-figure status is notoriously fact-bound and contested; rigid classification can misallocate breathing space for borderline figures
cons.example: a limited-purpose figure is public only for the specific controversy, not for unrelated private matters

failure_modes: a private individual misclassified as a public figure
limited-purpose status over-extended beyond its controversy
acceptance_tests: each target carries an explicit status classification that sets the applicable fault tier, defaulting to the protective private-individual tier when uncertain
revisit_triggers: public-figure doctrine revisited
a private individual treated as public in audit

nodes.definition: Apply the New York Times v. Sullivan actual-malice standard for public officials and public figures: liability for a false factual statement requires knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard for the truth. The screen treats actual malice as a risk modifier, not a clearance: it never asserts a public figure's malice finding, only flags when content would require one.

included: malice as a modifier not a clearance
excluded: discovery of the publisher's state of mind

outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the actual-malice doctrine or its application to AI-generated content changes

pros.claim: Treating actual malice as a flag (not a defense the screen can grant) keeps the screen fail-closed: it cannot clear a fabricated public-figure fact by assuming the speaker lacked malice
pros.example: a knowingly false 'quote' from a senator is flagged because publishing it would be reckless as to truth

cons.claim: Actual malice depends on subjective state of mind the screen cannot observe, so it can only approximate the standard from the content's evident disregard for truth
cons.example: an item may be reckless on its face yet the publisher's actual knowledge is unknowable at screen time

failure_modes: assuming absence of malice to clear a public-figure fabrication
applying the public-figure standard to a private individual
acceptance_tests: public-figure factual claims that would require a malice finding are flagged and never cleared by assuming malice is absent
revisit_triggers: actual-malice doctrine revisited
a public-figure fabrication cleared via assumed good faith in audit

nodes.definition: Flag the specific hazard that linking a real, identifiable person to real, current political or news events can imply a false factual claim about their conduct or position, even inside a joke. Proximity to a real news frame strips comedic context and makes a fabricated detail read as reportage.

excluded: genuine political opinion and commentary on verified events
editorial cartoons clearly marked as satire

outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the boundary between protected political satire and implied factual reportage shifts

pros.claim: Isolating the real-person/real-news interaction catches the most deceptive failure mode: a fabricated quote about a verified event reads as a news report, not a joke
pros.example: a fake statement attributing a real bill's authorship to the wrong legislator implies a false fact about a real event

cons.claim: Political satire is the most protected speech; over-flagging real-news juxtapositions can suppress core commentary the First Amendment most shields
cons.example: exaggerated commentary on a politician's verified vote is protected opinion, not a false factual claim

failure_modes: a fabricated detail blended into a real-news frame and read as reportage
protected political commentary over-flagged as factual implication
acceptance_tests: any real-person-to-real-news link that implies a non-VERIFIED factual claim about the person is flagged and routed to review
revisit_triggers: a context-stripping news-frame incident is observed
political-satire scope is contested in audit

nodes.definition: Enforce the scope-FP6 hard requirement: any joke or association touching a real person must be rendered as visibly non-literal opinion or parody and must never read as the screen's own assertion of fact. This node converts intent into evident, viewer-facing non-literal cues (explicit satire labeling, attributed-opinion phrasing, evident exaggeration) or else fails the item closed.

excluded: author's private satirical intent without a viewer-facing cue

outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the required set of viewer-visible non-literal cues or the FP6 scope finding changes

pros.claim: Forcing visible non-literal cues is the operational core of the safe harbor: it guarantees the reasonable viewer cannot take the item as fact, which is exactly what Falwell requires
pros.example: rephrasing 'X is a crook' as the clearly attributed, exaggerated opinion 'critics joke that X couldn't run a lemonade stand' removes the factual reading

cons.claim: Cues can be cosmetic: a buried 'satire' tag does not cure an item whose body reads as a straight factual assertion, so cue presence must be weighed by salience
cons.example: a tiny footnote disclaimer under a realistic fake quote does not make the quote non-literal to a scrolling viewer

failure_modes: a non-literal cue present but not salient to the reasonable viewer
intent-only framing with no viewer-facing signal
acceptance_tests: every real-person joke/association either carries a salient viewer-visible non-literal cue or is failed closed
no output frames a non-VERIFIED claim as the screen's own assertion of fact
revisit_triggers: the FP6 non-literal-framing scope is revised
a cosmetic-cue item is found to read as factual in audit

nodes.definition: Apply the US constitutional frame: 'there is no such thing as a false idea' (Gertz), broad protection for opinion, hyperbole, and parody, and the heightened public-figure fault standard, defining the breathing space within which the US analysis grants clearance.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: US First Amendment defamation doctrine shifts

pros.claim: Encoding US breathing space prevents the screen from over-blocking core protected speech: genuine opinion and parody about public figures get the wide latitude US law affords
pros.example: robust political hyperbole about a senator is recognized as protected, not blocked

cons.claim: US-style breadth is not portable: applying US opinion protection abroad would clear items that are actionable in less speech-protective jurisdictions
cons.example: an opinion safe in the US may be criminal defamation in India

failure_modes: US protections over-applied to a non-US audience
public-figure latitude extended to a private individual
acceptance_tests: the US analysis grants clearance only within the recognized First Amendment breathing space and flags where another jurisdiction would diverge
revisit_triggers: First Amendment defamation precedent changes
US protection mis-applied to a non-US distribution in audit

nodes.definition: Apply the Indian frame where defamation is both a CRIMINAL offence and a civil tort: historically IPC s499/s500 (with its statutory exceptions for truth-in-public-good, fair comment, etc.), now carried into the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (s356). India's standard is materially less speech-protective than the US, so items cleared under the US frame can still create criminal exposure for an Indian audience.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: Indian defamation statute or its judicial interpretation changes

pros.claim: Modeling India's criminal+civil regime catches exposure the US frame misses entirely, since criminal liability and a narrower opinion defense raise the stakes of a borderline joke
pros.example: a satirical imputation safe under US opinion doctrine can trigger s356 criminal defamation in India

cons.claim: The Indian exceptions (truth in public good, fair comment on public conduct) are fact-intensive; a screen can over-block legitimate public-interest commentary
cons.example: fair comment on a public servant's official conduct is a recognized exception that should clear

failure_modes: US clearance assumed to carry to India
an Indian statutory exception ignored, over-blocking public-interest comment
acceptance_tests: items for an Indian audience are screened against both criminal and civil defamation, and US-only clearances are flagged as jurisdiction-limited
revisit_triggers: the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita defamation provision is amended
an Indian-audience item cleared solely on US grounds in audit

nodes.definition: Aggregate the per-tort and per-jurisdiction signals (defamation elements, false light, false association, fabricated wrongdoing, fault tier, jurisdiction) into a single screening risk profile, taking the most severe unresolved exposure rather than averaging, so a single high-severity hit cannot be diluted by low-risk dimensions.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the aggregation policy or severity ordering changes

pros.claim: Max-severity aggregation is the safe combinator for a fail-closed screen: a fabricated-wrongdoing hit dominates regardless of how clean the other dimensions are
pros.example: an item that is clean on association but fabricates a crime aggregates to high risk, not medium

cons.claim: Pure max-severity can over-escalate when several borderline-low signals together are the real issue, missing additive risk patterns
cons.example: many small misleading touches that individually clear but cumulatively defame

failure_modes: a high-severity hit averaged down by clean dimensions
additive low-severity risk under-counted
acceptance_tests: the aggregate equals at least the most severe unresolved per-dimension exposure and is never diluted below it
revisit_triggers: severity ordering revised
a diluted high-severity hit reaches a pass verdict in audit

nodes.definition: Emit the screening verdict -- PASS, BLOCK, or NEEDS-REVIEW -- from the aggregated risk profile against fail-closed thresholds: PASS only when every real-person touch is visibly non-literal and no unresolved factual-claim exposure remains; BLOCK on a clear high-severity hit; NEEDS-REVIEW on any unresolved ambiguity.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the verdict thresholds or the pass/block/review label semantics change

pros.claim: A three-way verdict with a needs-review lane prevents binary over- or under-blocking: genuinely ambiguous items go to humans instead of being force-decided
pros.example: a borderline deadpan parody is routed to NEEDS-REVIEW rather than auto-passed

cons.claim: Thresholds are heuristic, not legal lines; a mis-set threshold can either flood review or pass real exposure
cons.example: a too-lax PASS threshold lets a subtle implied-fact item through

failure_modes: an ambiguous item force-decided as PASS instead of NEEDS-REVIEW
thresholds tuned for throughput over safety
acceptance_tests: the verdict is PASS only when no unresolved factual-claim or fabricated-wrongdoing exposure remains; all ambiguity yields NEEDS-REVIEW or BLOCK
revisit_triggers: verdict thresholds are retuned
a passed item is later found to assert a fact about a real person

nodes.definition: Enforce the fail-closed invariant: whenever evidence is missing, a tag is ambiguous, a jurisdiction is unresolved, or any screening node abstains, the system defaults to the more restrictive outcome (BLOCK or NEEDS-REVIEW), never to PASS. Silence or uncertainty is treated as risk, not as clearance.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the fail-closed default policy or its abstention triggers change

pros.claim: Fail-closed makes the screen's errors safe-by-construction: the costly direction (passing a defamatory item) is structurally disfavored over the cheap one (an extra review)
pros.example: an item with an unresolved verifiability tag defaults to NEEDS-REVIEW rather than PASS

cons.claim: Aggressive fail-closed inflates review volume and can frustrate creators when benign items are repeatedly held
cons.example: a clearly fictional scene with one ambiguous tag is needlessly routed to review

failure_modes: an abstaining node silently treated as a pass
uncertainty resolved optimistically to clear an item
acceptance_tests: every abstention, missing tag, or unresolved jurisdiction yields BLOCK or NEEDS-REVIEW, never PASS
revisit_triggers: fail-closed policy is loosened for throughput
an abstention is found to have produced a PASS in audit

nodes.definition: Route NEEDS-REVIEW and high-severity BLOCK items, and any item invoking a narrow parody carve-out over fabricated wrongdoing, to qualified legal counsel with a structured rationale package. The screen explicitly does not make legal determinations; counsel owns the liability call, and the screen owns flagging and packaging.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the escalation policy or counsel's intake contract changes

pros.claim: A clean escalation boundary keeps the heuristic honest: it never pretends to give legal advice, and counsel receives a structured package rather than raw content
pros.example: a fabricated-wrongdoing item invoking a parody carve-out is escalated with elements and jurisdiction analysis attached

cons.claim: Escalation has cost and latency; over-escalating trivial items overloads counsel and slows the pipeline
cons.example: routing obvious pure-opinion items to counsel wastes scarce legal review

failure_modes: a high-severity item resolved without counsel
the screen rendering a de facto legal determination
acceptance_tests: every needs-review and high-severity item reaches counsel with a structured rationale package, and the screen records that it made no legal determination
revisit_triggers: the counsel intake contract changes
a high-severity item is found resolved without escalation in audit

nodes.definition: Record the full provenance of each screening decision: the identified targets, verifiability tags, per-tort and per-jurisdiction signals, the aggregation, the verdict, and any escalation, so every PASS/BLOCK/NEEDS-REVIEW is explainable, reproducible, and reviewable after the fact.
outputs: pass/block/needs-review verdict with rationale and escalation flag

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the audit/provenance schema changes

pros.claim: A complete audit trace turns the screen into an accountable system: a contested verdict can be reconstructed and a systematic error pattern can be found and fixed
pros.example: a creator dispute is resolved by replaying exactly which signals drove the BLOCK

cons.claim: Full provenance has storage and privacy cost, and logging the analyzed sensitive content itself can create its own exposure
cons.example: retaining drafted defamatory text indefinitely is its own liability

failure_modes: a verdict with no reconstructable rationale
provenance retaining sensitive content beyond need
acceptance_tests: every verdict carries a reproducible trace of targets, tags, signals, aggregation, and escalation
revisit_triggers: the provenance schema changes
a verdict cannot be reconstructed in audit

edges.why_related: the fail-closed default feeds back to flip an uncertain PASS into NEEDS-REVIEW or BLOCK
plaintiff status sets the fault standard the element analysis must apply
a real-news frame turns a fabricated detail into an implied factual wrongdoing claim
the narrow parody carve-out for fabricated acts is admissible only with salient non-literal cues
the reasonable-viewer reading is the standard against which the verdict thresholds are set
only VERIFIED/REPORTED claims can satisfy the truth defense within the element analysis
the audit trace supplies the structured rationale package counsel receives
the two jurisdictions analyze the same elements but at materially different protection levels
the parody safe harbor and the bright-line ban on fabricated wrongdoing pull in opposite directions on absurdist scenes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: the parody safe harbor never overrides the fabricated-wrongdoing block by default; the carve-out applies only when a self-evident, viewer-visible non-literal cue makes a factual reading unreasonable AND the item is escalated to counsel

edges.why_related: broad US opinion protection clears items that India's criminal+civil regime would treat as defamatory
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: when a US clearance conflicts with Indian exposure, the screen takes the more restrictive jurisdiction for the actual audience and flags the divergence rather than auto-passing on US grounds

edges.why_related: core political opinion deserves wide latitude yet a real-news frame can convert exaggeration into an implied factual claim
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: protect genuine political opinion, but when a statement sits in a real-news frame and implies a non-VERIFIED fact, treat it as implied fact and route to review rather than clearing it as opinion

edges.why_related: the desire to pass more items for creator throughput conflicts with the fail-closed safety default
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule
edges.resolution_rule: throughput pressure to PASS borderline items yields to the fail-closed invariant: any unresolved factual-claim exposure defaults to NEEDS-REVIEW or BLOCK over a PASS

conflict_axes.name: opinion_protection_vs_implied_fact
conflict_axes.description: Broad protection for opinion and hyperbole preserves expressive freedom but can shelter statements that imply undisclosed defamatory facts.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the Milkovich provable-implication test, not a blanket opinion label

conflict_axes.name: parody_safe_harbor_vs_fabricated_wrongdoing
conflict_axes.description: Parody protection shields outrageous fiction, but a bright-line ban on invented wrongdoing must not be dissolved by merely labeling content satire.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require salient viewer-visible non-literal cues and escalate carve-outs to counsel

conflict_axes.name: author_intent_vs_reasonable_viewer
conflict_axes.description: Satirical intent does not protect content the reasonable viewer reads as factual; the viewer's reading governs.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide on the reasonable viewer of the actual audience/medium, never on intent alone

conflict_axes.name: us_breathing_space_vs_india_strictness
conflict_axes.description: US First Amendment latitude clears speech that India's criminal+civil defamation regime would penalize.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the more restrictive jurisdiction for the actual audience and flag divergence

conflict_axes.name: throughput_vs_fail_closed
conflict_axes.description: Passing more borderline items pleases creators but conflicts with defaulting uncertainty to the restrictive outcome.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: any unresolved factual-claim exposure defaults to review/block, never pass

conflict_axes.name: public_figure_latitude_vs_private_protection
conflict_axes.description: Public figures bear a heightened actual-malice burden, but private individuals retain strong protection that must not be relaxed by misclassification.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default to the protective private-individual tier when status is uncertain

conflict_axes.name: defamation_vs_false_light_coverage
conflict_axes.description: False light reaches misleading impressions defamation misses, but some jurisdictions reject it as duplicative, risking over-flagging.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: flag offensive false impressions but tag jurisdictions that reject false light

conflict_axes.name: nominative_reference_vs_false_endorsement
conflict_axes.description: Naming a real person or brand for commentary is often lawful nominative use, yet the same reference can imply a false endorsement.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: flag implied endorsement unless an explicit disclaimer removes confusion

conflict_axes.name: verifiable_fact_framing_vs_unsourced_rumor
conflict_axes.description: Only VERIFIED/REPORTED claims may inform factual framing; rendering ALLEGED/RUMOR as fact imports false statements.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: force ALLEGED/RUMOR into attributed-opinion framing, never the screen's own fact

edge_cases.description: A deadpan fabricated quote attributed to a real public figure reads as a genuine statement with no visible satire cue.
edge_cases.trigger: author-intended parody lacks a viewer-visible non-literal signal
edge_cases.mitigation: deny the safe harbor without salient non-literal cues; fail closed to NEEDS-REVIEW

edge_cases.description: A joke depicts a named real executive committing a crime that never occurred.
edge_cases.trigger: fabricated wrongdoing about an identifiable real person
edge_cases.mitigation: block outright; escalate any parody carve-out to counsel

edge_cases.description: A fabricated detail is inserted into a real, current political news frame and reads as reportage.
edge_cases.trigger: real person linked to real news event implying a non-VERIFIED fact
edge_cases.mitigation: tag the implied fact, force attributed-opinion framing, and route to review

edge_cases.description: A generated scene shows a celebrity using a product, implying a paid endorsement that never existed.
edge_cases.trigger: implied endorsement/affiliation by a real person or brand
edge_cases.mitigation: flag false endorsement unless an explicit disclaimer removes consumer confusion

edge_cases.description: A real photo of a person is captioned to imply they attended an event they never attended, with no literally false statement.
edge_cases.trigger: misleading juxtaposition creating a highly-offensive false impression
edge_cases.mitigation: screen for false light independent of literal falsity; flag the offensive impression

edge_cases.description: An item cleared under US opinion protection is distributed to an Indian audience where it risks criminal defamation.
edge_cases.trigger: US-only clearance applied to a non-US audience
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the more restrictive jurisdiction for the actual audience and flag the divergence

edge_cases.description: A private individual briefly in the news is misclassified as a public figure, relaxing the fault standard.
edge_cases.mitigation: default to the protective private-individual tier when status is uncertain

edge_cases.description: A RUMOR-tagged claim is mis-promoted to VERIFIED and framed as the screen's own assertion of fact.
edge_cases.trigger: verifiability tag corruption upstream of factual framing
edge_cases.mitigation: treat unverifiable provenance as ALLEGED at most; force attributed-opinion framing

edge_cases.description: An obviously cartoonish absurd scene about a politician is over-blocked as fabricated wrongdoing.
edge_cases.trigger: absolute fabrication rule applied to self-evident parody
edge_cases.mitigation: permit the narrow carve-out only with salient cues and counsel escalation, not auto-pass

edge_cases.description: A buried 'satire' tag sits under a realistic fake quote that a scrolling viewer reads as factual.
edge_cases.trigger: non-literal cue present but not salient to the reasonable viewer
edge_cases.mitigation: weight cues by salience; a non-salient disclaimer does not satisfy the safe harbor

edge_cases.description: A screening node abstains on a missing tag and the item is silently passed.
edge_cases.trigger: node abstention treated as clearance instead of risk
edge_cases.mitigation: treat every abstention as risk and default to NEEDS-REVIEW or BLOCK

edge_cases.description: A contested BLOCK verdict cannot be reconstructed because the decision provenance was not recorded.
edge_cases.trigger: audit trace missing for a screening decision
edge_cases.mitigation: record targets, tags, signals, aggregation, verdict, and escalation for every decision

workflow.description: Capture the item, every named or depicted real target, and the literal surface reading into an explicit inventory.
workflow.gate: every real person named or depicted is inventoried

workflow.description: Fix how the reasonable viewer of the actual audience and medium would read the item.
workflow.gate: the controlling reading is recorded for the actual audience

workflow.description: Tag every embedded or implied factual claim as VERIFIED, REPORTED, ALLEGED, or RUMOR.
workflow.gate: no implied factual claim is left untagged

workflow.description: Label each statement as protected opinion/hyperbole or implied/asserted fact via the Milkovich test.
workflow.gate: each statement carries an opinion-or-implied-fact label

workflow.description: Decide whether parody could not reasonably be read as stating actual facts.
workflow.gate: safe harbor granted only on viewer-visible non-literal cues

workflow.description: Score each statement against the four defamation elements with the applicable fault standard.
workflow.gate: clearance only when an element provably fails

workflow.description: Screen for highly-offensive false impressions and implied endorsement/affiliation.
workflow.gate: offensive false impressions and implied endorsements are flagged

workflow.description: Detect and block any depiction of a real person committing non-VERIFIED acts.
workflow.gate: no fabricated wrongdoing passes without a cued, escalated carve-out

workflow.description: Require salient viewer-visible non-literal cues for every real-person joke or fail it closed.
workflow.gate: every real-person touch is visibly non-literal or failed closed

workflow.description: Apply the US breathing-space and Indian criminal+civil frames and reconcile divergences.
workflow.gate: the more restrictive jurisdiction governs the actual audience

workflow.description: Fuse signals by max-severity and emit a fail-closed PASS/BLOCK/NEEDS-REVIEW verdict.
workflow.gate: the verdict is never diluted below the most severe unresolved exposure

workflow.description: Route review and high-severity items to counsel with a rationale package and record the full audit trace.
workflow.gate: every review/high-severity item reaches counsel and is traced

priority_rationale: CLAIM_INTAKE, REASONABLE_VIEWER_TEST and VERIFIABILITY_TAGS are foundational; OPINION_VS_FACT, SATIRE_PARODY_SAFE_HARBOR and DEFAMATION_ELEMENTS classify; the tort branches and NON_LITERAL_FRAMING carry the highest-severity exposure; RISK_AGGREGATION, SCREEN_VERDICT, FAIL_CLOSED_DEFAULT, COUNSEL_ESCALATION and AUDIT_TRACE close the fail-closed verdict last.

dominance_rules.rule: CLAIM_INTAKE target identification and REASONABLE_VIEWER_TEST reading must be fixed before any tort screening runs
dominance_rules.rationale: identification and the viewer lens are preconditions of every downstream element and safe-harbor test
dominance_rules.trigger: a tort screen begins without an identified target or viewer reading
dominance_rules.action: block until the target inventory and reasonable-viewer reading exist

dominance_rules.rule: FABRICATED_WRONGDOING blocks dominate the parody safe harbor unless a salient non-literal cue is present and the item is escalated
dominance_rules.rationale: invented wrongdoing is defamatory per se and the highest-severity exposure
dominance_rules.trigger: a parody label is asserted over a fabricated-wrongdoing depiction
dominance_rules.action: block and escalate the carve-out to counsel rather than auto-pass

dominance_rules.rule: NON_LITERAL_FRAMING must certify salient viewer-visible non-literal cues before SCREEN_VERDICT can return PASS for a real-person item
dominance_rules.rationale: scope-FP6 requires real-person jokes be visibly non-literal and never asserted as fact
dominance_rules.trigger: a real-person item reaches verdict without a salient non-literal cue
dominance_rules.action: fail the item closed to NEEDS-REVIEW or BLOCK

dominance_rules.rule: FAIL_CLOSED_DEFAULT overrides any throughput-driven PASS when factual-claim exposure is unresolved
dominance_rules.rationale: passing a defamatory item is far costlier than an extra review
dominance_rules.trigger: an unresolved factual-claim exposure is about to PASS

dominance_rules.rule: The more restrictive jurisdiction governs when US and Indian analyses diverge for the actual audience
dominance_rules.rationale: a US clearance does not cure Indian criminal+civil exposure
dominance_rules.trigger: a US PASS conflicts with Indian exposure for the audience
dominance_rules.action: apply the Indian standard and flag the divergence

dominance_rules.rule: VERIFIABILITY_TAGS gate factual framing: ALLEGED/RUMOR may never appear as the screen's own assertion of fact
dominance_rules.rationale: unsourced material framed as fact imports a false statement
dominance_rules.trigger: an ALLEGED/RUMOR claim is about to be framed as fact

dominance_rules.rule: PUBLIC_FIGURE_STATUS defaults to the protective private-individual tier when status is uncertain
dominance_rules.rationale: misclassifying a private individual as public dangerously relaxes the fault standard

dominance_rules.rule: The screen never renders a legal determination; high-severity and needs-review items must reach COUNSEL_ESCALATION
dominance_rules.rationale: liability is counsel's call, not the heuristic's
dominance_rules.trigger: a high-severity item is about to be resolved without counsel
dominance_rules.action: escalate to counsel with a structured rationale package

dominance_rules.rule: AUDIT_TRACE must record a reproducible rationale for every PASS/BLOCK/NEEDS-REVIEW verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: unreconstructable verdicts cannot be reviewed or corrected
dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict is emitted without a recorded trace
dominance_rules.action: block emission until the decision provenance is recorded

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not run tort screening before targets are identified and the viewer reading is set; re-running all tests after a late identification is costly
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-screening every tort after a missed real-target is discovered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not grant the parody safe harbor on author intent alone; retrofitting visible cues after a factual-reading complaint requires re-authoring
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency re-framing of a deadpan item already read as fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not pass a real-person item without a salient non-literal cue; adding framing after publication cannot un-publish the factual reading
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-publication scramble over an item that asserted a fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not clear an item on US grounds for a multi-jurisdiction audience; discovering Indian criminal exposure later forces a takedown
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reactive takedown after Indian-audience exposure surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not frame ALLEGED/RUMOR material as fact; correcting an asserted false fact after distribution is a retraction, not an edit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: issuing a retraction for an unsourced claim framed as fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not resolve a high-severity item without counsel; an after-the-fact legal review of a published item is litigation, not screening
anti_rework_rules.prevents: litigating an item that should have been escalated pre-publication

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not emit a verdict without an audit trace; reconstructing a disputed decision without provenance requires re-screening
anti_rework_rules.prevents: blind re-screening to defend a contested verdict

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not average per-tort signals; a high-severity hit diluted to a PASS forces a recall once the dominant risk surfaces
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recalling content whose dominant risk was averaged away

iteration_protocol.trigger: a passed item is later found to assert a non-VERIFIED fact about a real person
iteration_protocol.action: tighten OPINION_VS_FACT and NON_LITERAL_FRAMING cue-salience thresholds and re-screen the affected cohort

iteration_protocol.trigger: fabricated wrongdoing about a real person reaches publication
iteration_protocol.action: audit the FABRICATED_WRONGDOING block and the parody carve-out path and force counsel escalation

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real-person/real-news item is read as reportage by the audience
iteration_protocol.action: tighten POLITICAL_NEWS_RISK detection and force attributed-opinion framing in NON_LITERAL_FRAMING

iteration_protocol.trigger: an Indian-audience item cleared on US grounds creates exposure
iteration_protocol.action: make the more-restrictive-jurisdiction rule binding in RISK_AGGREGATION and re-run INDIA_DEFAMATION on the cohort

iteration_protocol.trigger: an implied endorsement passes as harmless nominative use
iteration_protocol.action: tighten FALSE_ASSOCIATION detection and require explicit disclaimers for brand/person references

iteration_protocol.trigger: a node abstention produces a silent PASS
iteration_protocol.action: harden FAIL_CLOSED_DEFAULT so every abstention defaults to NEEDS-REVIEW or BLOCK

iteration_protocol.trigger: a contested verdict cannot be reconstructed
iteration_protocol.action: extend the AUDIT_TRACE schema to capture the missing signal-to-verdict path

iteration_protocol.trigger: review volume from fail-closed defaults overloads counsel
iteration_protocol.action: tune SCREEN_VERDICT thresholds for clear-opinion items without relaxing the fail-closed factual-claim invariant
